You shouldn't have to bet on which AI model wins to build a successful AI company.


That's a principle behind what Ishaan Sehgal and his team are building at Omnara.


Ishaan and his co-founder have known each other since preschool. They got into Y Combinator on their first attempt with an idea to automate code documentation, but quickly realized their conviction was elsewhere.


They saw an opportunity in the infrastructure required to bring AI agents into production.


Building an agent is only part of the equation. Developers also need to host it, store conversations, manage sessions and ensure reliable execution. Each of these requirements adds engineering complexity that takes time away from building the actual product.


Omnara handles that infrastructure through a single API.


What makes its approach particularly interesting is the emphasis on developer independence.


As an open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API, Omnara is model-agnostic, supports self-hosting and allows developers to bring their own compute.


It's a strategic decision rooted in Ishaan's observation that model providers are increasingly competing with the very companies they serve.


Developers are already using Omnara to automate lead generation, introduce virtual teammates into Slack and embed agents directly into their products.


Ishaan believes that even if AI models stopped improving today, there's still a decade's worth of applications to build.


While the industry debates which AI model will dominate, Ishaan and his team are building the infrastructure that allows developers to succeed regardless of which one does.
